If token is [robot] and you are
in a [computer] Room, you may use
the Robot.

When you remove the last card from this deck
Queen is dead. Remove her Miniature and all
the tokens from the discard from the game.

When you draw a Queen token from the bag
nothing happens and remove that token from
the game.

Make a Noise Roll
and Hibernate.

confidentlyVisible: The file is a sparse texture atlas with disconnected science-fiction board panels on a transparent or black field.
Most labels are upright in the file, while the OBJECTIVE CHOICE panel near the lower-left edge is rotated sideways.
A vertical numbered track visibly runs from 1 through 14.
The central chamber is labeled HIBERNATORIUM and contains six radial corridor branches.
Large region letters A, B, and C are visible.
A red-bordered panel is headed QUEEN'S HEALTH CARDS.
Separate labeled areas read QUEEN'S HITS and EGGS.
Several LIFE SUPPORT labels and machinery symbols are visible.
A robot-shaped white glyph and a cyan computer-screen glyph appear in the Robot instruction panel.
MISSION TASK labels a large empty rectangular slot.
uncertainties: This is a multi-component texture atlas rather than one conventional card, so no single semantic title, card face, or card back applies.
No single rotation makes every meaningful text panel upright: most typography is upright, but the OBJECTIVE CHOICE panel is rotated 90 degrees relative to the rest.

The exact visual identity of several board-local symbols is outside the supplied canonical glossary, including the orange three-lobed symbol, radial arrows, yellow numbered triangles, and objective-choice comparison glyphs; they are not semantically mapped.
The purple glyph in the Robot instruction is mapped to [robot] and the cyan monitor glyph to [computer] based on confident morphology, but the purple background treatment is component-local.
Some texture elements extend to or are clipped by the image boundaries.
The atlas as a whole has no unambiguous semantic filename stem supported by one visible title.
